name: aomega-m3-pretzel-onesided-theta-dressing
description: The one-sided Gaussian dressing of the pretzel's residue families, derived from GGM (108)/(109) in closed q-Pochhammer form, its collapse to Part 14's pair monomial, and the dressed weight-1 fusion.
verdict: DERIVED: the one-sided Gaussian dressing of a residue family is a THETA, not a monomial — theta(-q^{-1/2} x_F; q) = (x_F;q)_inf (q/x_F;q)_inf by GGM (108) — and Part 14's monomial x_F^{-A} is only what the PAIR collapses to, via (x;q)_inf = (1-x)(qx;q)_inf. Splitting it before the collapse gives, for the pretzel at A = 2: diagonal weights D_1 D~_1 = X^-2 and D_2 D~_2 = X^+2 (G1, Part 14 reproduced) but CROSS weights D_1 D~_2 = D_2 D~_1 = 1 (G2). So the dressing weights the diagonal and the cross terms of the weight-1 bilinear DIFFERENTLY, which is outside the uniform per-family monomial class that Part 14 tested and Part 15 excluded — that is why neither found it. It is exactly Z/2-equivariant (G3), so Part 16's symmetry-adapted basis and its (4,1,1) grading are unchanged and the weight-1 slot is still the antisymmetric one. Transporting GZ Obs 3.9 to the DRESSED basis: index match = False; branches with q^0 row = 1: none. AND, measured: W^2 = s(x) - 3 EXACTLY, and every row of the dressed fusion is a rational function of the ADJOINT WEIGHT s(x) alone, with denominator a power of (s-3) — q^0 = -s/(s-3), q^1 = 2(s^2-1)/(s-3) — so it lives in exactly the ring GGM's Stokes matrices live in, which is what #7333's Z/2 grading predicts for integer powers of q. What separates it from the index is therefore a NORMALISATION in that ring, and that is #7333's named missing input too: the two routes converge on one gap. Sharper still (G7): WITHOUT the 1/W^2 the same bilinear lies in Z[s] exactly — integer coefficients, no denominator, the ring GGM's (188)/(307) entries live in — with q^0 row s(x) against the index's 1.

assertions.name: G1-the one-sided theta factors reproduce Part 14's PAIR monomial exactly: D_1 D~_1 = X^-2 and D_2 D~_2 = X^+2 (so this split is consistent with the established result, not a new convention)
G2-the CROSS products carry weight ONE: D_1 D~_2 = D_2 D~_1 = 1
G3-the dressing is exactly Z/2-equivariant, D_1(1/X) = D_2(X) — so Part 16's symmetry adaptation survives it unchanged, and the weight-1 slot is still the antisymmetric one
G4-diagonal and cross weights DIFFER (X^-2, X^+2 vs 1), so the dressing is not a uniform per-family monomial reweighting — it is outside the class Part 14 tested and Part 15 excluded
T1-the DRESSED weight-1 element's fusion reproduces the derived rotated index to q^3 under some branch and zeta identification
T2-at least one branch's dressed q^0 row equals 1 (the index's constant term), which the BARE Part 16 fusion did not give
G5-the antisymmetric coordinate squares to the adjoint weight shifted: W^2 = s(x) - 3 exactly, so Part 16's division by W^2 is a division inside the adjoint-weight ring, not an extraneous factor

G7-without Part 16's 1/W^2 the dressed weight-1 bilinear lies in Z[s] EXACTLY — a polynomial in the adjoint weight with integer coefficients, no denominator — which is precisely the ring GGM's (188)/(307) Stokes entries live in; its q^0 row is s(x) where the index's is 1, so the whole residual gap is one normalisation

G6-every row of the dressed weight-1 fusion is a rational function of the ADJOINT WEIGHT s(x) alone, denominator a power of (s - 3) = W^2 — the same ring GGM's Stokes matrices live in, which is what sibling #7333's Z/2 grading predicts for integer powers of q
